items.summary: Permission to act, successful execution and money received are different milestones. A control can protect backing without giving every holder time—or a funded route—to leave.
Permission and usable money are separate dependencies. Follow the policy decision, the operator’s action and the external asset release all the way to the holder.
A loan-pool share, a fund redemption and an eligible holder’s payout are different claims, controlled by different parties. Follow the asset across each boundary before treating it as usable cash.
Subject guides, a complete research catalogue and visual explanations. Historical report routes retained.
Why backing, legal claims, privileged actions, collateral pricing and exit liquidity must be assessed together—and why the person facing the deadline matters.
Custody, settlement and release gates between a protected asset and usable funds.
Issuer eligibility, signed authorization, privileged submission and the atomic settlement boundary.
Fixed queued USDe, reward and timer consequences, exact units and the separate controller execution paths.
Dated control settings, source/deployment cross-checks and the unresolved owner-controller link.
Direct, staked and nested/lending exits with a bounded system-risk picture.
